Container.Name: Stackyard
Container.Overview: A self-hosted homelab dashboard you actually want to look at.[br][br]Most dashboards are a wall of numbers and charts. Stackyard is the opposite: a calm, launcher-style grid of app tiles, folders, and a small number of genuinely useful widgets. Built to be glanced at a hundred times a day without feeling cluttered.[br][br]Everything is set up from the browser. Add app tiles, group them into folders, arrange pages, and drop in widgets for the services you already run. Widgets cover Docker, system health, downloads, media, backups, network and more.[br][br]Runs as one container with no external database and no runtime dependencies. Configuration and uploaded icons persist in the two paths below.[br][br]Note: most homelab services live on private addresses. The Allow Private IPs setting below is on by default so links and widgets pointing at your other containers work. Turn it off to keep the SSRF guard enabled.

Container.DonateText: If Stackyard is useful to you, you can buy me a coffee.
Container.Changes:
### 1.25.0 - 2026-11-28
### Added
- Show an inline completion in phone search that Return opens.
- Add a request id to every API answer and its log line.
- Add a link to password help on the sign-in screen.
- Show the error code and request id under a failed test in Settings.
- Give the Settings tab bar icons a short spring when a tab is picked.
### Changed
- Bend the Settings tab bar on phones like iOS: the glass lens lifts on any press, the bar swells, and the selected colour follows the lens.
- Keep drag-to-pick on the Settings tab bar with Reduce Motion on, as a plain pill.
- Fade the Settings page between light and dark instead of switching at once.
- Redesign search on phones: the field grows from the Search pill, follows the keyboard, and results show a Top Hit card with Apps and Folders sections.
- Show only names that start with the query in phone search, when any do.
- Close an empty search with the field's x on phones.
- Let `LOG_LEVEL` override the Logging Level setting.
- Refuse a language or log level Stackyard cannot use instead of dropping it.
- Balance seven icons optically so they look centred in their buttons and plates.
- Balance the side padding of pill buttons next to their round ends.
- Show an ocean coast wallpaper in the demo and the install screenshots.
- Replace the two App Title switches in Appearance with one Show App Names menu.
- Require the current `_rev` in API config saves.
### Fixed
- A press on the Settings tab bar lens right after picking a tab is no longer ignored.
- The Settings tab bar lens no longer settles 1 px off its tab.
- Rotating the phone while holding the Settings tab bar no longer picks the wrong tab.
- Reset the search overlay's edges when the window crosses to the desktop layout while search is open.
- Stop an older version from rewriting a settings file saved by a newer one.
- Explain a dashboard or Settings page whose scripts cannot start, instead of loading forever.
- Keep a widget's working frame when a refresh of it fails to start.
- Log where a broken settings file stops being valid JSON.
- Warn at start about environment values Stackyard cannot use.
- Import the usable files when one of several import files cannot be read.
- Keep an icon or wallpaper upload going after the session expires.
- Refuse a file over the upload limit before sending it.
- Show a rejected widget key in widget settings instead of an expired session.
- Send an open dashboard to sign-in when its session ends.
- Explain a sign-in or save refused because a reverse proxy rewrote the Host header.
- Name the reason a settings save or import was refused.
- Ask to wait when sign-in is busy, and say when the device is offline.
- Reload an open dashboard after Stackyard is updated.
- Name the real cause of a failed connection test instead of suggesting the container name.
- Show a translated reason for a failed app health check, and name a socket proxy failure instead of a missing container.
- Show certificate, rate limit and permission failures on widgets.
- Refuse a config save that has no revision instead of overwriting the dashboard.
- Show an error when a health check is turned on with nothing to check, instead of saving it as off.
- Load the install manifest behind a sign-in proxy such as Authelia.
- Count the current hour in Technitium DNS totals.
- Show "Last test failed" instead of negative speeds when the latest speed test failed.
- Show a CPU temperature in a remote temperature slot saved without a sensor.
- Tell volumes of one series apart on a Kavita reading list shelf.
- Keep rain, snow, storm, Mostly Clear and Tornado weather icons clear of the card's top edge.
- Stop Safari from highlighting drop-down option text in Admin.
- Stop Settings menus cutting off the chosen value on narrow screens.
- Stop the Unraid template saying most homelabs need Allow Private IPs.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port the dashboard is reached on.

Config.Name: Config Storage
Config.Description: Dashboard configuration. Keep this, or every setting is lost on update.

Config.Name: Icon Storage
Config.Description: Icons you upload for your app tiles.

Config.Name: Allow Private IPs
Config.Description: Let the editor test apps, badges and widgets on private addresses, and load a wallpaper link from one. Saved apps, badges and widgets reach private addresses either way. Set to false to keep the SSRF guard on.

Config.Name: Docker Socket Proxy URL
Config.Description: Optional. Address of a Docker socket proxy, for the Docker widgets. Example: http://socket-proxy:2375

Config.Name: Trust Proxy
Config.Description: Optional. Set to true behind a reverse proxy that terminates HTTPS, so the sign-in cookie is marked HTTPS-only.

Config.Name: Node Options
Config.Description: Node heap cap. Keep it near half the --memory limit in Extra Parameters, and raise both together.
